# While it builds {.divider background-color="#CC0000"}

[Two ideas to have ready when it's done: memory and skills]{.eyebrow}

## Claude forgets. Files don't.

::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
[`CLAUDE.md`: you write it]{.card-title}

- A file in your folder
- Read at the start of **every** session
- Rules and facts it can't know: definitions, dates, house rules
- *"Add this to CLAUDE.md: …"*, or `/init` for a first draft
:::

::: {.card}
[Auto memory: it writes it]{.card-title}

- Notes Claude saves as it learns your project
- On by default; you'll see *"Saved 1 memory"*
- Kept in your home folder, one set per project
- `/memory` shows and edits both kinds
:::
:::

::: {.muted style="margin-top:20px"}
Keep `CLAUDE.md` short: every line is read every time. (The old `#` shortcut is gone; just ask.)
:::

## Skills: instructions with a name

<div class="type shell" style="font-size:0.62em">.claude/skills/house-style/SKILL.md &nbsp;&nbsp;→&nbsp;&nbsp; /house-style</div>

::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
[You run it]{.card-title}

Type `/house-style`, like any command.
:::

::: {.card}
[Claude runs it]{.card-title}

When what you ask matches the skill's description, Claude can pick it up on its own.
:::
:::

::: {.muted style="margin-top:20px"}
Custom commands and skills are now the same thing; old `.claude/commands/` files still work. Put a skill in your
project's `.claude/skills/`, or in `~/.claude/skills/` to use it everywhere.
:::
